title: Arithmetic subgroups of isotropic absolutely almost-simple Q-groups have norm-controlled bounded generation by standard Q-rank-one subgroups
author: Dave Witte Morris
work: Quasi-Isometric Bounded Generation  by Q-Rank-One Subgroups
source_version: Official SIGMA 16 (2020) article 012, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2020.012; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: The proof strengthens geometric generation to a uniformly bounded number of rank-one factors while retaining polynomial norm control. It orders relative root directions, reduces successive unipotent coordinates using arithmetic big-cell representatives, and proves the crucial factor norm bounds through rational lowest-weight functions. A Levi-factor and anisotropic-torus reduction closes the induction, so the bounded product conclusion is not merely the existing word-length comparison theorem.

source_check.note: Read the full main proof and its local dependency chain: commensurability/isogeny reductions, Lemma3.7 Levi decomposition, lowest-weight big-cell description and rational norm bounds, and all of Lemma4.1 including finite representative construction and quantitative estimates. The cited Lubotzky-Mozes-Raghunathan argument is actually reproduced with the required bounded-step modification; standard arithmetic lattice, Bruhat and Tits results are identified background. Select the explicitly assumed absolutely almost-simple Q-group case of Assumption3.6 with the full Sections3-4 proof. Do not count S-arithmetic, restriction-of-scalars or infinite-center extensions as separate variants. Source approval supplied only by exact frozen root input; no new source/difficulty decision or mathematical referee.

retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Theorem1.2 with the explicit simplifying Assumption3.6: isotropic absolutely almost-simple algebraic Q-group and any arithmetic subgroup Gamma. Bounded generation has exactly Definition1.1 scope: fixed r,C, finite exceptional Gamma_0 and finitely many standard connected Q-rank-one root subgroups, with each factor either exceptional or lying in a subgroup intersection and satisfying the stated logarithmic norm bound. No SL(n,Z)-specific n^2-n count, arbitrary S-arithmetic or infinite-center assertion is added.
